Definition: from G4754; an armament, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops (more or less extensive or systematic):--army, soldier, man of war.
BiblicalUsage: Armies are the hosts sent out by kings, and the last armies are heaven's. The king in the parable sends forth his armies and destroys the murderers, the armies in heaven follow the rider on the white horse, clothed in fine linen, and the beast gathers his armies to make war against Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the armies of heaven follow a King who needs no army, and the armies gathered against Him are gathered for their fall.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
